name: Biscuit
breed_facts: Golden retrievers are energetic and love having a job to do, whether that's fetching, swimming or just running around the garden. They genuinely need regular exercise to stay happy, so they thrive with owners who can commit to daily walks and outdoor time. That's exactly why Biscuit would make such a great match for you!
browse_description: Biscuit is a Golden Retriever in the prime of life, full of energy and always keen to be doing something. He came to us when his previous family could no longer meet his exercise needs and it's easy to see why needs an active home, he simply has too much love and energy to still for long. Every day starts the same way for Biscuit: straight to the door, tail going, hoping for a walk. He's happiest outdoors, whether that's a proper walk, a game of fetch in the garden or a splash about if there's water nearby. Once he's had his exercise, though, he settles down easily and is just as happy to flop by your feet for the evening. Biscuit gets on brillantly with people of all ages and has lived with children without any issues. He's sociable with other dogs too and would likely enjoy having canine company in the home, though it isn't essential. He needs an owner who can genuinely commit to daily exercise, ideally more than one walk a day given his energy levels. Without it, he can become a little eestless and vocal. A garden would be a bonus but isn't required, so long as regular outdoor time is guaranteed.

name: Buddy

Bred originally to follow scents for hours at a time, he's got real stamina and an enthusiasm for the outdoors that shows in everything he does. Give Buddy a garden or a park and he'll happily spend the whole time working every inch of it nose first, tail wagging the entire time. Once he's had his fill of sniffing and exploring, he's content to settle down at home, often choosing a spot near his favourite person to curl up. Buddy is friendly and easygoing with people, including children and has lived alongside other dogs without any issues, generally enjoying the company. He can be a little vocal when excited or when he picks up an interesting scent, which is worth knowing for households in close prxomity to neighbours. He needs regular walks and time to explore outdoor to stay content and avoid boredom related behaviours. A secure garden would suit him well, though isn't essential provided his exercise needs are met elsewhere.
